money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Cash report: Australia's rules require a report for physical currency of A$10,000 or more (or the foreign equivalent) moved into or out of Australia, with no limit on the amount carried. Bearer negotiable instruments such as cheques have no dollar threshold and must be disclosed. The page doesn't say how it applies on trips between the mainland and this external territory, so confirm with Australian Border Force.

laws.rule: Cocos (Keeling) Islands is an Australian external territory: Commonwealth laws apply unless excluded, and Western Australian laws apply as 'applied laws' unless an Ordinance repeals, suspends or modifies them. No consolidated list of applied laws is published, so check WA law and the territory's Applied Laws Ordinance for a specific rule.

items.text: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands Act 1955 (Cth) applies Western Australian laws on the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, and all Australian Government laws apply except where explicitly excluded. Drug offences therefore follow the applied Western Australian law and Commonwealth law; the territory penalties themselves were not read. Australian citizens carrying drugs into Australia face Australian customs law.

items.text: The Commonwealth Marriage Act 1961 extends to the Territory of Cocos (Keeling) Islands (section 8). Marriage is open to a person aged 18 or over. A person aged 16 or 17 needs an order from a judge or magistrate, given only in exceptional circumstances (section 12). A marriage valid in Australia is valid in the external territories (section 73).

When the Cocos (Keeling) Islands community voted to join Australia in 1984, the Australian Government committed to respect the community's religious beliefs, traditions and culture. Ask locally, particularly on Home Island, about dress and conduct.
